rule: Allow only machine-consumed fields and sentinels, real source/packaged equality, parser/runtime/security behavior, or user UI/error copy; forbid authored prompt, SKILL, rule, and TOML prose plus headings, order, negative wording, and length contracts.

allowed.rationale: Asserts that a recovered LSP diagnostic is returned to the user after the unavailable-extension cache clears; the diagnostic is user-visible error feedback, not authored agent instructions.
BUNDLED_PERSONA_SENTINEL is fixture-only marker data used to prove that the selected bundled rule body crossed the runtime injection seam.
Instructions from: is the stable delimiter emitted and re-read by transcript-rule-filter to detect already-injected rule records; this assertion covers deduplication state rather than rule prose.
Compares the machine-consumed hook commands read from the packaged hooks.json with the component CLI entrypoints, proving the shipped hook wiring invokes the real runtime commands.
allowed.expected: <expression:[ `node "${pluginRoot}/dist/cli.js" hook session-start`, `node "${pluginRoot}/dist/cli.js" hook user-prompt-submit`, `node "${pluginRoot}/dist/cli.js" hook post-tool-use`, `node "${pluginRoot}/dist/cli.js" hook post-compact`, ]>

allowed.rationale: Pins malformed-frontmatter recovery: parseRule must preserve the complete malformed input as its body instead of dropping bytes while reporting a diagnostic.
alwaysApply: true is a machine-consumed rule frontmatter field whose presence proves the bundled rule remains an unconditional parser input.
git_bash is the exact MCP tool identifier that the bundled Windows rule must reference; it is a machine-facing tool name rather than natural-language wording.
OMO_CODEX_GIT_BASH_PATH is the runtime environment-variable identifier shared by installer and Git Bash execution surfaces.
Compares the bundled Codex directive file with the prompts-core Codex source, preventing the shipped runtime copy from drifting from its canonical source.
The package build script is machine-executed metadata; its ordered sync, clean, and bundle commands determine whether the shipped CLI contains the generated directive.
allowed.expected: node scripts/sync-directive.mjs && node -e "require('node:fs').rmSync('dist',{recursive:true,force:true})" && bun build src/cli.ts --target node --format esm --outfile dist/cli.js

allowed.rationale: directive.md is a packaged runtime filename required by the build and fallback loader, not a claim about the directive text.
Compares the hook context with the pointer builder result, proving the existing-skill runtime branch returns the generated pointer for the supplied absolute path.
create_goal is the exact registered tool identifier required in the compact pointer bootstrap and is machine-facing sentinel data.
Proves the missing-skill fallback returns the canonical ULTRAWORK_DIRECTIVE value rather than an independently authored duplicate.
Proves the null-skill fallback returns the canonical ULTRAWORK_DIRECTIVE value rather than an independently authored duplicate.
user_prompt_submit is a serialized steering-source enum value consumed by the CLI parser and ledger model.
OMO_ULW_LOOP_STEER is the runtime sentinel that selects the structured steering parser.
annotate_ledger is a machine-consumed steering kind token accepted by the parser and persisted in structured audit output.
accepted is a structured steering result/status token used to prove the hook mutation succeeded, not authored instruction prose.
directive.md is an npm package file entry needed by the standalone fallback runtime.
hook user-prompt-submit is the machine-executed CLI subcommand in hooks.json and proves the packaged event is routed to the intended handler.
name: ulw-loop is the machine-consumed SKILL frontmatter identity used by Codex skill discovery.
display_name is Codex skill-picker UI metadata; the asserted value is displayed to users rather than injected as agent instruction prose.
short_description is Codex skill-picker UI copy used to present the skill to users.
allowed.expected: short_description: "Goal-like ultrawork loop for systematic decomposition"

allowed.rationale: search_terms is a machine-consumed Codex skill-discovery metadata field.
ulw-loop is the canonical machine-facing search alias for the skill discovery index.
user-prompt-submit is the implemented hook-channel CLI token documented by the component and consumed by command dispatch.
Compares the ulw-loop bundled directive with the ultrawork component source so the standalone shipped fallback cannot drift.
Compares the extracted ulw-loop pointer template with the ultrawork source template, proving the two runtime copies remain byte-identical.
name: ulw-research is machine-consumed SKILL frontmatter proving post-install skill synchronization materialized the expected skill identity.
approval_policy = "never" is a machine-consumed Codex security setting written when explicit autonomous permissions are requested.
The version-stamped statusMessage is displayed by Codex while the hook runs and verifies packaged version rewriting of user-visible status copy.
frontend/SKILL.md is a packaged file-path invariant proving the installer retained the root skill while excluding nested reference skills.
approval_policy = "never" verifies the end-to-end installer writes the requested autonomous Codex security policy into config.toml.

forbidden.rationale: Pins negative wording inside an authored bundled rule. The runtime does not parse shell: "bash" as a field here, so the prose prohibition must not be a test contract.
Pins the authored Windows rule wording by requiring the prose token WSL; this is not a parser, security check, or machine-consumed field.
Pins the authored Windows rule wording by requiring the prose token System32; the exact instructional wording is not a runtime contract.
Pins an example executable path embedded in authored rule prose. The rule body is model guidance and no runtime parser or launcher consumes this literal path.
Pins the full authored additionalContext instruction for a created thread. Thread-id extraction and hook JSON shape can be tested without contracting this prompt wording.
forbidden.expected: THREAD ID thread-123: CALL codex_app.set_thread_title NOW. USE THE REAL TASK/ROLE.

forbidden.rationale: Pins the full authored additionalContext instruction for a JSON-string thread response; the relevant parser behavior does not require exact prompt prose.
forbidden.expected: THREAD ID 019ef350-ee78-72a3-bd5e-e40cebc3d814: CALL codex_app.set_thread_title NOW. USE THE REAL TASK/ROLE.

forbidden.rationale: Pins the full authored pending-worktree instruction, including negative and ordered wording, instead of only the extracted identifier and runtime branch.
forbidden.expected: PENDING WORKTREE ID remote-control:env:test-worktree: WORKTREE THREAD IS NOT READY YET. DO NOT bind-thread OR SEND THE MEMBER BOOTSTRAP UNTIL A REAL THREAD ID EXISTS. THEN CALL codex_app.set_thread_title USING THE REAL TASK/ROLE.

forbidden.rationale: Pins the authored Goal: heading inside a generated agent instruction. Advancement is already asserted through the structured next.goal id and plan state.
Use $ulw-loop is authored default-prompt prose in skill metadata, not a machine field or user-facing status/error string.
